purpose: Declared persistence requirements. Saved-table reopen does not qualify journal/crash recovery or repeated performance comparisons.

data.schema: Six non-null I64 columns: id, customer, symbol, day, qty, price
data.seed_profile: Existing experiment.py generator, Random(20261117); preserve its CSV byte lengths and SHA256 manifest
data.live_profile: Existing ingestion-contract.json deterministic append formula; IDs never reused
data.input_equivalence: Same seed fixture, append IDs/bodies, grouping queries and complete ordered output on both engines

saved_table.rayforce: Explicit native splayed/partitioned save and reload; in-memory insert is not a persisted acknowledgement
saved_table.duckdb: Persistent DuckDB file using the native C API, committed writes and explicit checkpoint where the case requires it
saved_table.claims: A saved-table reopen does not qualify live WAL recovery or physical power loss
saved_table.atomicity_scope: Immutable input fixture. Separate Rayforce table saves are not a multi-table atomic live backup; DuckDB CTAS commits before the explicit checkpoint.

synchronous_journal.rayforce: Native synchronous IPC request path with journal opened in sync mode; RAYFORCE_NO_FSYNC=0 before initialization. Verify effective environment, native status and actual replay
synchronous_journal.duckdb: Persistent file, default durable transactions and WAL; no fsync weakening to match another profile
synchronous_journal.claims: Expect zero acknowledged row/body loss after a fenced process/container SIGKILL and retained-volume native recovery. Power-loss durability remains unqualified

asynchronous_journal.rayforce: Separate observation profile with explicit sync watermark; reconcile later ACKs and ambiguous intents independently
asynchronous_journal.comparison: Do not pool with the synchronous profile or label weaker durability as a faster equivalent

consistency: One authoritative writer per persistent dataset; verify fresh reads of committed rows, native lock behavior and the declared API boundary. No distributed, HA or multi-process concurrent DuckDB writer claim.
atomicity: Successful logical row/batch acknowledgements require complete expected columns. General failed-operation/OOM rollback and multi-request atomicity are not assumed; preserve intents and reconcile partial/ambiguous effects.
idempotency: No automatic mutation retries; unique IDs are application-generated, not assumed to be server-side deduplicated. A timeout or closed connection is not proof that no mutation applied.

reference_client.application: C++ with CMake and upstream native C APIs
reference_client.independent_reader: Required for live failure cases; use native Rayforce IPC and make the DuckDB application boundary explicit before measuring. Adapter/RPC/FFI costs must be labeled
reference_client.status: Rayforce native IPC adapter and independent live-writer/reader controller implemented; DuckDB live adapter remains unimplemented. Saved-table profiles remain separate from the live failure results.
reference_client.scope: The future live journal/fault profile. Offline snapshot C API calls currently use the existing 600-second whole-process bound, without per-call cancellation.

resources.initial_profile: 1 CPU / 4 GiB charged memory, swap disabled, per engine. Existing historical results keep their original captured limits.
resources.required: CPU utilization/core-seconds, process RSS and cgroup memory, logical/allocated disk and native persisted bytes, compression at a named layer, block read/write bytes and available I/O counters; include import, save, query, replay and repair phases

correctness_gates: Validate every old/new row in ID order against the independent canonical CSV oracle, including earlier ACKs
Persist an fsynced external intent/ACK witness outside the failed storage
Prove old-owner exit before replacement; verify native replay and readable rebuilt state
Test snapshot plus journal tail, a second snapshot/restart, and no duplicate replay
Keep writers/readers live through operational faults; saved-table tests alone do not meet this gate
Distinguish torn final frames from corruption inside intact frames; retain original evidence and native diagnostics
performance_gate: Correctness/recovery first. Three fresh-process trials with matched input, query results, durability and resource budgets; report actual monotonic durations, trial spread, native storage/compression and per-phase resource costs. OS-cold behavior requires an isolated owned environment or supported cache controls; never clear shared host caches.
